## Goal
Make the choice of state-law letter in `letters.py` smarter, using the existing `law_matrix` data (read only): choose the statute template by the person's state, fall back to the generic request when the state has no right-to-delete law, and never cite a law that does not apply.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
1. Table test: CA, VA, CO, TX, OR pick their own template; a state with no matrix entry picks the generic one.
2. State input is tolerant: 'ca', 'CA ', 'California' resolve the same; an unknown value falls back to generic, never raises.
3. The citation text in the rendered letter comes from the matrix entry, not a literal in `letters.py`.
4. Public function signatures stay as they are (additive helpers only).
5. Existing letter tests pass unchanged.

This is Codex code-lane work (owner, 2026-11-09): fix and improve the listed module(s) directly, with tests; don't xfail a bug you can fix here. No contract changes: public function signatures, `src/freemyid/models.py`, `interfaces.py`, schema files, `--json` shapes and documented CLI output stay as they are (additive helpers inside the listed files are fine). If the work turns out to need a contract change, stop and say so in VENDOR_STATUS.md "Questions for the owner". Fake data only, offline (fake fetchers, no network), Windows-safe paths in tests (`tmp_path`, `pathlib`, no `/tmp`). Typed, ruff-clean, small diff. Line numbers, where cited, are from main at the time of writing; re-check them.
